name: boygenius
label: Interscope
lede: Julien Baker, Phoebe Bridgers and Lucy Dacus booked a tour before they had a song and cut six in four days at Sound City. Four years later they made The Record in one month at Rick Rubin's studio, and it went No. 1 in the U.K.

eras.title: Three solo artists on the same circuit
eras.text: Before there was a band, Baker recorded alone in Memphis, Dacus finished a debut in Virginia and Bridgers took meetings in Los Angeles. A run of opening slots in 2016 put them in the same dressing rooms.

years.h: Baker records Sprained Ankle alone and puts it on Bandcamp
years.p: 6131 Records released it afterward. Critics reached for words like "heartbreaking" and "hypnotic".
years.xp: Wikipedia describes the album as self-recorded, put up on Bandcamp first and widely praised on release. Baker signed to Matador Records in 2017.

years.cap: Baker at The National's Homecoming festival, Cincinnati
years.src: Rolling Stone: Boygenius on The Record · Exclaim!: The Magic of boygenius · Wikipedia: Julien Baker and Phoebe Bridgers with Lucy Dacus Tour
years.h: Dacus opens for Baker in D.C. and tears out a page with her email on it
years.p: Baker found Dacus in the dressing room reading Henry James's The Portrait of a Lady. Bridgers met Baker a month later.
years.xp:
Exclaim! says Dacus ripped a blank page out of a book to give Baker her email address. Baker told Rolling Stone she thought "We're gonna be friends." Rolling Stone puts Baker's meeting with Bridgers a month later, and Exclaim! has the three trading emails about literature.

Wikipedia's page on the 2018 tour has it differently: Dacus and Bridgers each opened for Baker separately, and Baker introduced them to each other only in 2018.

years.h: No Burden gets Dacus a Matador contract
years.p: Before it, she'd left the film program at Virginia Commonwealth University and was working as a photo editor.

years.src: Wikipedia: Better Oblivion Community Center · Wikipedia: Phoebe Bridgers
years.h: Conor Oberst hears Bridgers is a fan and invites her onstage at the Bootleg
years.p: At a secret showcase at the Bootleg Theater in Los Angeles, [[Conor Oberst|0eee89dc-7d86-4a15-97be-011652c49288]] had her play, then asked for her unreleased songs.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, Oberst suggested at the time that they "start a band and sound like the Replacements". Bridgers opened his European tour in 2017.

years.h: Bridgers's Stranger in the Alps comes out on Dead Oceans
years.p: Tony Berg produced, and strong reviews made her a name outside L.A.

years.h: Baker brings in strings for Turn Out the Lights
years.p: Recorded at Ardent Studios in Memphis with producer Calvin Lauber, it has the orchestral parts her debut didn't, and it's her Matador step.

eras.title: The tour went on sale before the songs existed
eras.text: The plan was a seven-inch for the merch table. They booked the tour first, went to Sound City, and made six songs in four days that turned into a band.

years.src: Wikipedia: Julien Baker and Phoebe Bridgers with Lucy Dacus Tour · Exclaim!: The Magic of boygenius
years.h: The tour goes on sale before there's a song
years.p: Baker, Bridgers and Dacus had no music written together. The plan was a single 7-inch for the merch table.
years.xp: Wikipedia's tour page says the trio booked the tour before recording anything. Exclaim! says being booked on a fall 2018 triple bill is what led them to record a 7-inch to sell at merch.

years.cap: Bridgers at The Crocodile, Seattle, July 2018
q: We set out to make one song, and made six.
years.src: Wikipedia: Boygenius (EP) · Wikipedia: Boygenius · Rolling Stone: Boygenius on The Record
years.h: Four days at Sound City, and every hire is a woman
years.p: They self-produced at Sound City Studios in Van Nuys, California. Each brought one finished song and one unfinished idea.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the recording to four days in June 2018. The three decided to hire only women for the sessions. Bridgers described the plan to Rolling Stone this way: "We set out to make one song, and made six."

years.h: The boygenius EP arrives two weeks early, on Matador
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.3. Three songs had come out Aug. 21: "Bite the Hand", "Me & My Dog", "Stay Down".
years.xp: The planned release date was Nov. 9. Wikipedia lists the Pitchfork review at 8.3 (reviewer Dayna Evans) and Metacritic at 84, and says NPR Music ranked it 12th of 2018 despite the EP format.

years.cap: Dacus on the boygenius tour, November 24, 2018
years.src: Wikipedia: Julien Baker and Phoebe Bridgers with Lucy Dacus Tour · The Fader: boygenius tour and EP
years.h: Nashville's Ryman opens a four-week run that ends in Los Angeles
years.p: Each played a solo set, then all three came out for the EP. The last night was Nov. 30.
years.xp: Wikipedia and The Fader agree on the run, Nov. 4 to Nov. 30, 2018. The dates included Brooklyn Steel, Toronto's Danforth Music Hall, Chicago's Thalia Hall and Minneapolis's First Avenue.

years.src: NPR Music: boygenius Tiny Desk Concert
years.h: At the Tiny Desk, all three admit they're nervous
years.p: Host Bob Boilen asked if it got easier the second or third time. All three said no. They played "Souvenir", "Me & My Dog" and "Ketchum, ID".
years.xp: Each had done a Tiny Desk alone before; Baker had done two. NPR calls this their first time there together, and Boilen called them "one of this year's best surprises". NPR published the video Nov. 15.

eras.title: Everybody goes solo, nobody quits
eras.text: The band went quiet but not away: backing vocals crossed between each other's solo records, Bridgers made a second band with Oberst, and one demo in a shared folder started everything again.

years.cap: Bridgers and Oberst as Better Oblivion Community Center, Showbox, Seattle, March 18, 2019
years.h: Bridgers and Oberst drop Better Oblivion Community Center without warning
years.p: The band grew out of the secret L.A. showcase where they met in 2016. Dead Oceans released it.

years.h: Bridgers's second album, Punisher, collects four Grammy nominations
years.p: They included Best New Artist at the 63rd Grammys. Dacus and Baker sing on tracks.

q: Can we be a band again?
years.src: Rolling Stone: Boygenius on The Record · Exclaim!: The Magic of boygenius · Variety: boygenius record tour interview
yt: boygenius: Emily I'm Sorry (official music video)
years.h: A demo of "Emily I'm Sorry" lands in a shared folder
years.p: After Punisher, Bridgers sent the song to Baker and Dacus through Google Drive with that question attached.
years.xp: Rolling Stone says Bridgers sent the demo after the Covid lockdown, with all three nervous about showing interest. Exclaim! places the shared-folder message after Punisher, and Variety dates the album's origin to the week after Punisher.

years.h: The EP demos go on Bandcamp and raise more than $23,000
years.p: The money went to Downtown Women's Center in L.A., OUTMemphis and Mutual Aid Distribution Richmond.

years.h: Little Oblivions: Baker on drums, bass, keyboards, mandolin and banjo
years.p: It became her first Billboard 200 top-40 album.

years.h: Three years after the tour, they headline a San Francisco benefit
years.p: The Bread and Roses benefit is their first full show together since 2018.

eras.title: A month at Rubin's, then No. 1
eras.text: One month at Rick Rubin's studio, a deal with Interscope and three videos directed by Kristen Stewart. By spring the debut album was No. 1 in the U.K. and No. 4 in the U.S.

years.cap: Bridgers at Marymoor Park, Redmond, Washington, August 24, 2022
years.src: Rolling Stone: Boygenius on The Record · Wikipedia: The Record (Boygenius album) · Wikipedia: Not Strong Enough
years.h: They move into Rick Rubin's Shangri-La for most of January
years.p: Co-producer Catherine Marks was there too, and Sound City in Van Nuys was the second studio. [[Jay Som|3b910f7b-018f-408f-950b-47e02d2ce305]] played bass on "Not Strong Enough" and Carla Azar played percussion.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone says they spent nearly all of January 2022 recording and living at [[Rick Rubin|07aebfa0-55d6-47e0-a284-12330e3eae0d]]'s Shangri-La in Malibu. Wikipedia lists Sound City as the second studio, and Marks as co-producer.

Rolling Stone also says the album was the first major-label release for any of the three.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Record (Boygenius album) · Wikipedia: Boygenius
years.h: Three singles land at once, with Kristen Stewart behind the videos
years.p: "$20", "Emily I'm Sorry" and "True Blue". Kristen Stewart directed the videos, which premiered together March 30 at the El Rey Theatre in Los Angeles.

years.h: "Not Strong Enough" gets a video that's just a day out in L.A.
years.p: Filmed around Los Angeles County and edited by Bridgers's brother Jackson. It was the last song finished for the album.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, the video shows the band spending a day together around Los Angeles County, including the Santa Monica Pier and the Getty Villa. The song was the sixth of twelve tracks.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Record (Boygenius album) · Album of the Year: boygenius, the record · Rolling Stone: Boygenius on The Record
yt: Not Strong Enough on Jimmy Kimmel Live
years.h: The Record goes No. 1 in the U.K. and No. 4 on the Billboard 200
years.p: Interscope released it. Pitchfork's Cat Zhang gave it 8.2 and ranked it No. 16 for the year; Metacritic scores it 90.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists Pitchfork at 8.2 (Cat Zhang) and Metacritic at 90 from 26 critics. Album of the Year's aggregate is 88 from 40 reviews, and it ranks its own Pitchfork entry at 82.

Charts, per Wikipedia: No. 1 in the U.K., Ireland and the Netherlands, No. 4 on the Billboard 200. The cover echoes Crosby, Stills & Nash's debut, and Rolling Stone says the band's name refers to overconfident men praised for every thought.

years.src: Variety: boygenius record tour interview · Wikipedia: Boygenius
years.h: Coachella gives the new songs their first big room
years.p: Variety reported a warm-up show in Pomona before the festival. The tour ran April to August with Carly Rae Jepsen, Bartees Strange, Claud and others opening.
years.xp: Wikipedia adds Broken Social Scene and Illuminati Hotties to the openers, plus five fall dates with Palehound, Samia and Muna. Bridgers said it was "100 percent" their greatest tour experience.

years.h: At Pryzm in Kingston, "Emily I'm Sorry" runs into "Cool About It"
years.p: A U.K. date on the tour, captured on YouTube.

years.h: The Rest collects four songs cut that May in Tennessee and Van Nuys
years.p: "Black Hole", "Afraid of Heights", "Voyager" and "Powers", recorded at Blackbird and Sound City. Pitchfork scored it 7.5.
years.xp: It reached No. 50 on the Billboard 200 and No. 6 on Top Alternative Albums, per Wikipedia. Pitchfork called it aglow with the sense of triumph around the group's recent history.

years.src: Under the Radar: boygenius on SNL
years.h: Chalamet hosts, and boygenius plays and turns up in a sketch
years.p: It came a day after their Grammy nominations.

years.h: NME puts The Record first for 2023, Rolling Stone second
years.p: Variety and the Independent agreed with NME; Billboard sided with Rolling Stone. Pitchfork ranked it No. 16.

eras.title: Two days before the Grammys, a goodbye
eras.text: The band said it was going away for the foreseeable future. They won anyway, and all three are back on their own records.

years.src: Wikipedia: Boygenius · Stereogum: Boygenius Win Their First Grammy Awards
years.h: The Smell, a small Los Angeles room, hears the hiatus first
years.p: The band told the crowd it was an indefinite hiatus, two days before the Grammys.
years.xp: NME quotes the rest of the message: "This is our last show, and we're feeling it." Per Wikipedia, Dacus said the final song was just the closing track, and she was "not convinced" the hiatus would be permanent.

years.cap: Dacus of boygenius at The Gorge, Washington
years.src: Stereogum: Boygenius Win Their First Grammy Awards · NME: Boygenius' Julien Baker at 2024 Grammys · Wikipedia: Lucy Dacus · Wikipedia: Not Strong Enough
years.h: Three Grammys, two of them for "Not Strong Enough"
years.p: The song won Best Rock Song and Best Rock Performance; The Record won Best Alternative Album. Bridgers also won on SZA's "Ghost in the Machine".
years.xp:
Wikipedia describes the group as the first all-female band to win Best Rock Song and Best Rock Performance. "Not Strong Enough" lost Record of the Year to Miley Cyrus's "Flowers".

Baker told NME: "Music is the language I used to find my family since I was a kid."

years.h: Dacus's Forever Is a Feeling comes out on Geffen
years.p: It debuted at No. 16 on the Billboard 200, her highest-charting solo album.

years.h: Six years after Punisher, Bridgers releases Lost Weekend
years.p: Her third album, on Dead Oceans, and her first full solo album since 2020.
